snippet.title: I found these EV chargers at the National Trust!
snippet.description:
I’ve discovered new RAW Charging EV charge points in my Tesla Model 3 Performance at RHS Garden Rosemoor and National Trust Arlington Court in North Devon, exactly the sort of destination EV charging that makes owning an electric car in rural areas so much easier.

In this video, I take a closer look at these new AC destination chargers, show you where they are located, how the charging process works, and what payment options are available. Unlike rapid charging, these chargers are ideal for longer stays: plug in, enjoy a walk around the gardens or estate, and return to your car with useful extra range added.

For EV owners exploring Devon, visiting National Trust properties, RHS gardens, or simply looking for convenient public charging away from motorway services, installations like these could make a real difference to everyday electric car ownership.

I’ll be covering:

⚡ The new RAW Charging facilities at RHS Garden Rosemoor and Arlington Court
⚡ How to start a charge and pay
⚡ Why slower AC charging works so well at visitor attractions
⚡ Whether these chargers make days out in an EV more practical
⚡ My real-world experience using destination charging in rural North Devon

RAW Charging is rolling out EV charging across visitor destinations including National Trust properties and RHS gardens, helping drivers charge while they spend time at places they already want to visit. Arlington Court is listed with four Type 2 connectors, while RHS Garden Rosemoor forms part of RAW Charging’s wider RHS rollout.

snippet.title: This Old House | It Never Rains In California? (S32 E21) | FULL EPISODE
snippet.description:
At the project house, exterior work has been delayed due to four weeks of record-setting rains in Southern California. Inside, Host Kevin O'Connor finds plaster expert Alfonso Garcia installing custom foam forms to create a tray ceiling that replicates the existing detail in the house. Once the forms are in place, they are covered with plaster.

SUBSCRIBE to This Old House: http://bit.ly/SubscribeThisOldHouse.

Master carpenter Norm Abram visits cabinetmaker Larry Bucklan at his shop in the nearby neighborhood of Frogtown to see how work is progressing on the kitchen cabinets. The boxes and drawers are made off-site in Orange County, but Larry's crew carefully makes the doors and the custom end panel for the refrigerator. Back at the house, Larry builds a toe kick to receive the base cabinets. Upstairs, Alfonso shows Kevin the "cat face" plaster technique he is using on the walls to replicate the original plaster style. This technique provides a combination of open and closed finishes—after the finish coat is applied, but before it sets up, he goes back over it with his trowel, leaving closed and open patches. Some areas of the finished coat are smooth, while others are rough, a condition known as "cat faces." In the original part of the house, Kevin finds a new stain on the ceiling of the dining room and a large hole in the ceiling of the front entry. Due to leaks and damage from the rains, site supervisor Angel Leon explains that although the homeowners had been hoping to be able to keep the existing roof on the main house, it looks as if it's going to have to be replaced after all.
